name: Pan-nationalism
summary: Pan-nationalism holds that a people with shared language, ancestry, culture or civilization, spread across several states, should see itself as one nation and move toward unity, whether as a single state or a federation or union. It stands above ordinary nationalism in scale: Pan-Slavism, Pan-Germanism, Pan-Arabism, Pan-Africanism and Pan-Turkism are the best known forms. Adherents agree on unity across borders and, in the anti-colonial strands, on opposing outside domination, but disagree widely on economics, democracy, religion and race.
scope: The profile represents the family as a whole, centred on four documented strands: Pan-Slavism (Kollar, Safarik, Palacky, 1848 Prague Congress), Pan-Germanism (Jahn, Arndt, Pan-German League), Pan-Arabism (Aflaq and the Ba'ath, Nasser) and Pan-Africanism (Nkrumah, the OAU/AU). It is the shared core of unity across borders, not any one strand's economics, so most statements outside nation, borders, unity and anti-domination are low-confidence or neutral. It excludes Pan-Islamism, which is religious rather than ethnic, and Nazi expansionism beyond its pan-German roots.

keyFigures.name: Jan Kollar
keyFigures.role: Slovak poet whose writings argued the Slavs form one people with a shared culture, a founder of Pan-Slavism.

keyFigures.name: Michel Aflaq
keyFigures.role: Co-founder and chief ideologist of the Ba'ath Party, advocating a single Arab nation.

keyFigures.name: Kwame Nkrumah
keyFigures.role: Ghana's first leader and the leading advocate of a continental union government for Africa.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The ideology concerns the scale of the nation, not welfare policy; Arab socialists and Nkrumah's followers would agree while Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives would not.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No pan-national doctrine addresses wage law; adherents split along their regime's economic line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The strands with state-building programmes (Ba'ath, Nkrumah's Pan-Africanism) favoured state planning, though Pan-Germanism and Pan-Slavism had no fixed economic doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Ba'athism and Nkrumah's followers favoured state control of major resources, while other strands such as Pan-Germanism were not committed to it, so adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a pan-nationalist question; positions follow each strand's economic politics.

unions-good.rationale: Pan-nationalism has no labour doctrine; strands range from socialist unionism to nationalist corporatism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are not central; Arab socialist strands curtailed them while Pan-German conservatives upheld them.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed by the core ideology; adherents vary with their economic orientation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to welfare levels; it is carried by both left and right movements.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ba'ath socialism offered profit-sharing and state control rather than worker ownership, and most strands do not endorse collective workplace ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology's regimes were often security-minded but this is not a defining position.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the mostly culturally conservative, nation-building character of the main strands; not stated in sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The ideology does not address speech law and its strands diverge.

strong-leader.rationale: Nasser and Nkrumah were charismatic unifiers and Pan-Germanists looked to a strong state, but democratic Euro-Slavs and others reject this, so adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: Pan-nationalism aims to build a larger state or union, so it is the opposite of anti-statism.

empower-police-military.rationale: No doctrine on domestic policing; unity projects stressed common defence (Nkrumah) but this is not about funding police.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the generally traditionalist cultural stance of the main strands; not documented.

decide-locally.rationale: Pan-nationalists want authority pooled at a continental or pan-national level; Nkrumah wanted a union government with executive powers over defence, foreign policy and currency.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the mostly culturally conservative strands; Pan-Slavism and Pan-Germanism were Romantic movements, but the sources do not state it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the culturally conservative character of most historical strands, not directly documented.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from typical conservative nationalist leanings; the sources are silent.

more-religion-public.rationale: Strands disagree: Ba'athism favoured a secular state, Pan-Slavism's Stur favoured Orthodoxy, and Pan-Germanism had Lutheran and anti-Catholic currents.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Pan-Africanism arose from resistance to slavery and colonialism and would agree, but Pan-Germanism and Pan-Slavism have no such concern.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the generally traditional outlook of the main strands.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pan-nationalism rests on a shared cultural heritage (language, ancestry) that it seeks to preserve and raise to a broader identity, as Kollar and Zaydan stressed shared culture and language.

gradual-change.rationale: Pan-nationalists generally pursued rapid revolutionary unification, as Aflaq's call for revolution and Nkrumah's 'unite now or perish' show.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; strands vary, and the focus is on unifying existing kin populations.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pan-nationalists want regional unions (African Union, Arab League) but are wary of Western-led global bodies, so the UN question splits them.

free-trade.rationale: Nkrumah's programme was common continental planning with shared markets and neo-colonial dependence criticised; inferred general scepticism of open global trade.

nation-first.rationale: Pan-nationalism puts the interests of the enlarged national community first, though it is wider than a single country and sometimes cooperative internationally.

open-borders.rationale: Pan-nationalists want borders open within the kin group but not worldwide; the global statement is read literally.

limit-growth.rationale: The development-oriented strands favour growth and unification; inferred, not stated.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for most of the historical strands.

revolution-justified.rationale: Aflaq called for a revolution spreading from country to country to produce Arab unity, and Nkrumah linked unity to completing anti-colonial struggle; other strands were more moderate (Palacky's autonomy within Habsburg lands).

central-planning.rationale: Nkrumah urged common continental planning and Ba'athists state control, but Pan-Germanism and Pan-Slavism had no such program, so adherents split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Arab socialist and African socialist strands would accept it; others are indifferent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nkrumah's push for a continental common market and planning aimed at escaping dependence implies economic protection of the bloc; inferred rather than stated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nkrumah proposed common continental planning of industry and agriculture and the Ba'ath charter state control of major resources; other strands are silent.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Ba'ath socialism kept wages with profit-sharing; no pan-national strand seeks to abolish money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nkrumah explicitly proposed a central bank and single currency for Africa.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; some nationalist strands favoured corporatism, others did not.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Ba'ath Party was a vanguard that favoured one-party rule, while Euro-Slavism and the 1848 Slavic Left favoured democracy, so adherents are split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Palacky backed the Habsburg monarchy, Stur the Russian tsar and Serbs the Karadjordjevic dynasty, whereas Arab and African pan-nationalists were mostly republican; the family is split.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1848 Slavic Left and Euro-Slavism favoured democracy, but Ba'athism favoured a vanguard party and Pan-German League circles were authoritarian.

workers-councils.rationale: No pan-national strand bases power on workers' councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Pan-nationalism aims to unite states rather than split them; Aflaq condemned existing Arab divisions and Nkrumah wanted unity to heal boundary disputes.

natural-rulers.rationale: Pan-German racial thought believed in hierarchy, but other strands do not; split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Unity was pursued through revolution, war and conquest in several strands (Pan-German expansion, Ba'athist coups, the Arab struggle with Israel).

war-builds-character.rationale: Pan-Germanist circles glorified war and expansion, but Pan-Africanists and Euro-Slavs did not, so adherents are split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Ba'athism and Zaydan stressed language and nation over religion, while Stur's Slavism centred on Orthodoxy; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Pan-nationalism bases identity on ethnicity, language or region and not scripture; Pan-Islamism is the religious rival Arab nationalists contrast themselves with.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Nkrumah proposed a common continental defence system and high command, and pan-national projects centre on public state structures.

military-superiority.rationale: Not a defining position; the unified bloc's strength was desired but superiority over rivals is not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ethnic pan-nationalisms such as Pan-Germanism and ethnic Pan-Slavism hold that peoples of shared ancestry form one nation, but Pan-Africanism and civilizational strands define the bloc more widely, so the answer is moderate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Aflaq blended Marxism with nationalism, but treated nation as primary; the family is not committed either way.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Pan-Africanism arose from resistance to enslavement and colonisation and Pan-Arabism opposed Sykes-Picot, so reparations are consistent, though the sources do not explicitly demand them.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-nationalism unites peoples of shared heritage across borders, and the pan-regional strands (Pan-Africanism, Pan-Arabism) treat a shared civilization as a basis for union, though Pan-Islamism itself is a different case.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The ideology subordinates individual advantage to the national community; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on the collective nation; not stated directly.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Nkrumah and the Ba'ath sought industrial development, though Romantic Slav and German thinkers had some anti-modern currents.

restore-past-order.rationale: Some strands look back to a lost unity (Pan-German Reich, Slavic common heritage) while Pan-Africanism and Ba'athism are forward-looking revolutions; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents follow a nationalist principle of unity rather than judging policy on results alone; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Revolutionary Ba'athists favoured action beyond elections, whereas the 1848 Slavic congress, Euro-Slavs and AU diplomacy worked through institutions.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Pan-nationalism is a modern state-building project and has no primitivist strand.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a position of any strand; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist strands might agree in principle, but the ideology does not address it.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist strands might agree, others not; not a defining question.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Ba'athism and Nkrumah's followers drew on Marxism, others did not, so adherents split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Aflaq's Ba'athism took from Marxism but rejected the class-based doctrine, putting nation first.

collective-farming.rationale: Ba'ath land reform favoured redistribution; collective farming is not a pan-national position.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nkrumah's neo-colonialism critique attributes dependence to capitalist powers, but the thesis of inevitable inter-imperialist war is not a pan-national tenet.

taxation-theft.rationale: Pan-nationalism seeks strong common states or unions and has no libertarian strand.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Pan-nationalism centres on the collective rights of peoples and nations, though it does not necessarily deny individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Nkrumah proposed a common defence system and unity movements regard defence of the larger nation as a duty; inferred, not stated.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The ideology builds large unions with loyalty to the nation, so it is not exit-minded; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The ideology treats the state as the instrument of the nation, not as a business; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Aflaq tied freedom to socialism and unity, but other strands lack such a position.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Pan-German League thinkers embraced racism and Pan-Africanists affirm shared African descent without hereditarian claims about ability; the family is split.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; some nationalist movements favoured corporatist structures but it is not defining.

total-state.rationale: The ideology wants a unifying state but not a total state directing all life; Aflaq stressed liberty as central.

national-rebirth.rationale: Aflaq's Ba'ath is literally the 'resurrection' of the Arab nation and many pan-national movements frame unity as national awakening; not all strands speak of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pan-German expansionism (Drang nach Osten, Heim ins Reich) and Arab unity aspire to enlarge a national state, but Pan-Africanism and Euro-Slavism reject conquest, and the Wikipedia article says Lebensraum is not itself pan-nationalist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not a feature of modern pan-national movements; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Pan-nationalism is a modern nationalism, and Pan-Africanism arose from resistance to enslavement.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism emphasises a collective interest but this is not a statement of its epistemology.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Pan-Arabism was largely framed against Zionism and Israel; other strands (Slavic, German, African) have no stance, so the answer rests on the best-documented strand.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Pan-Africanism links the African diaspora to the continent and kin-based nationalism supports co-ethnic ties; inferred rather than stated as a legal right.

revive-national-language.rationale: Zaydan and Arab nationalists promoted Modern Standard Arabic and Stur codified Slovak, so language revival is a common nationalist tool; not defining for every strand.

national-self-determination.rationale: Pan-nationalists claim a right of the whole people to a state, as in Aflaq's party constitution on a single Arab state, though they apply it to the larger group, not to each small nation.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that citizenship might extend across the kin group.

class-collaboration.rationale: Aflaq put nation above class and Arab socialism sought national unity rather than class conflict; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Romantic pan-national movements prized the shared cultural heritage in philology and folklore.

dominated-front.rationale: Pan-Africanism and Pan-Arabism strongly opposed Western political and economic involvement and formed bodies like the OAU and Arab League; Euro-Slavs differ.

workers-nation.rationale: Ba'athism and Nkrumahism put the nation, not an international working class, first, though they are not exclusively working-class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; strands diverge from conservative to modernising.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-Islamism would agree but it is not the pan-national core.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Pan-Africanism arose against racial subjugation and most strands do not seek segregation law, though Pan-German League racists would differ.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist-influenced strands might agree, but nationalists generally see the state as the nation's instrument.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of this kind is not part of any pan-national strand; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Aflaq's slogan of an Arab nation with an eternal mission suggests a message, but it concerns culture and not spreading a form of government; strands split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Pan-nationalists blame colonial powers and divided elites, but corruption of elites generally is not a defining claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Nazi-linked racism inherited from Pan-German thought is not representative of the mainstream of the family.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream pan-national strands do not discourage mixing; only the Pan-German League racists would.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Pan-Africanism and Arab nationalism assert the equality of their peoples against colonial hierarchy, though early Pan-German racism did not; adherents of the mainstream agree.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Aflaq held that revolution must spread across Arab countries until unity; this parallels the claim that change cannot stay within one border, though not about socialism per se.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Pan-Arabism treated Israel as a colonial intrusion and Pan-Africanism opposes settler colonialism; other strands have no stance.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Ba'athism was secular, Stur's Slavism was Orthodox; split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state claim that is outside the pan-national doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democratic strands agree, but Ba'athism held that a vanguard leads even against majority opinion; split.

population-transfer.rationale: Not a stated position of the mainstream family; Pan-German expansionism had ethnic-cleansing aspects but it is not central.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Pan-German thinkers framed peoples as competing, but Pan-Africanists and Slavic unity thinkers stress solidarity; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-colonial pan-nationalists frame unity as ending domination by foreign powers, which fits this idea; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Ba'ath Party was a Leninist vanguard but most other pan-national movements were not, so adherents split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Nkrumah blames neo-colonial structures and disunity for poverty, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Pan-nationalists claim kin similarity strengthens unity, but they also try to merge diverse existing states; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not a pan-national position; inferred from state-building emphasis.

party-controls-media.rationale: Ba'athism governed through one party, others did not, so adherents are split.

party-commands-army.rationale: A Ba'athist practice, not a pan-national tenet.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Ba'athism used democratic centralism, but this is not a family position.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a pan-national issue; Stur's Orthodoxy and Pan-German Lutheranism diverge.

clerical-rule.rationale: Arab nationalists put nation above religion and Aflaq said the party is not a religious party; pan-Islamism is a rival.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalists support their nation in war; the statement is Leninist. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romantic nationalists celebrated peasant folk culture, but this is not a stated pan-national position.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Pan-national movements were often founded by scholars, philologists and intellectuals like Kollar and Zaydan.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Pan-African and Arab nationalists affirm equal worth, whereas Pan-German racists asserted hierarchy; split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic pan-nationalisms like Pan-Germanism tie nationhood to ancestry and Heim ins Reich claimed co-ethnics abroad; civilizational strands differ.

minority-language-support.rationale: Austro-Slavism sought cultural autonomy but pan-national movements also promote a common language; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism emphasises shared custom, so inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nkrumah criticised neo-colonial dependence and African unity movements called for debt relief; inferred from anti-dependency stance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nkrumah said the struggle does not end with national independence and tied dependence to neo-colonial control.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Ba'athism and some strands accepted authoritarian development while Euro-Slavs and others did not.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nkrumah emphasised collective self-reliance and warned of neo-colonial aid, so adherents split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Nkrumah proposed a central bank as an instrument of common planning, not an independent one; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Pan-Arab opposition to Israel and Pan-German expansionism lean toward refusing, but Pan-Africanists favour settling boundary disputes through union; split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Ba'ath charter says the nation's wealth belongs to the nation and Arab socialism subordinated property to national interest; others are silent.

collective-defense.rationale: Nkrumah proposed a common defence system and African high command, and the Arab League and OAU embody collective security among kin states.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Secular Ba'athists would agree while Orthodox-centred Slavs would not; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Since unity is the goal and Aflaq rejected division as anathema, preventing separation is consistent; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nkrumah proposed that states keep their sovereignty while pooling defence, foreign policy and currency, and Austro-Slavism sought autonomy within a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not a feature of the main pan-national strands; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; racialist strands favoured innate nature, others not.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the constitutional unions pan-nationalists propose.

leader-cult.rationale: Nasser and Nkrumah attracted mass leader praise but the ideology itself does not prescribe it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not a Ba'athist or pan-national doctrine; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Ba'ath charter included land reform, but other strands lack such a program.

refugee-return.rationale: Pan-Arabism supported return of Palestinian refugees as a core cause; other strands lack a position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Germanism claimed Germans abroad through Heim ins Reich and Pan-Slavism and Pan-Arabism seek to unite co-nationals across borders; this is the core of the family, though Wikipedia distinguishes it from irredentism by scale.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Arab nationalists put ethnicity and language over religion and Aflaq's party was not religious; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Secular Ba'athists and Nasserists did not impose it; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Nkrumah explicitly proposed a single currency and central bank for Africa, and union projects involve pooling of monetary policy.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Austro-Slavism sought autonomy for Slav lands in the Habsburg state, but others wanted a common state; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Pan-nationalists generally seek unity of the kin group across borders rather than a minority staying and fighting for rights in each state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist-influenced strands lean this way but Romantic nationalist strands attribute change to ideas and identity.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Pan-Africanists stress collective self-reliance and Nkrumah wanted common continental planning and market to escape neo-colonial dependence; the statement's colonies clause fits less well.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Ba'athists plotted coups, but Aflaq spoke of committed revolutionaries rather than guerrilla foco; split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Republican Pan-Arab and Pan-African strands would abolish it while Palacky and Habsburg loyalists would not; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Pan-nationalism builds a shared identity from common history and culture, so teaching it from the group's perspective is consistent.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Pan-Africanism and Pan-Arabism arose in opposition to colonial tutelage, though Pan-German and Russian Pan-Slav expansion had paternalistic features.

patriotic-education.rationale: Pan-nationalists seek to teach a broader shared national identity, so pride in the shared flag and heritage fits.

public-money-creation.rationale: Nkrumah proposed a central bank and common currency, but there is no doctrine on private bank money creation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Russian Pan-Slavs used the movement to project influence in the Balkans, while Euro-Slavs and Pan-Africanists oppose such neo-imperial influence; split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Nkrumah wanted collective self-reliance and a continental market but not complete delinking; adherents split.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from collectivist nature.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Pan-Arabists condemned Sykes-Picot as an imposed partition and Nkrumah called colonial boundaries a festering sore; the claim that they lack force today is the unity argument.

elective-rulers.rationale: Republican strands agree while monarchist Pan-Slavs did not; split.

minority-veto.rationale: The ideology prizes unity over individual veto; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Palacky-era liberals might agree but later pan-nationalists were not defined by this; split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Pan-nationalism is an activist political movement aimed at changing state boundaries.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Nkrumah linked continued economic dependence to neo-colonial control by foreign powers and Pan-Africanists oppose outside economic involvement.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed; this is a communist-party question.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Pan-Africanism stresses collective self-reliance, with advocates seeing continental solidarity as letting Africa provide for its own people.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pan-Germanism and Pan-Arabism have irredentist elements, but the family distinguishes itself from irredentism and Pan-Africanists seek to settle boundaries via union; split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Pan-Africanism and Pan-Arabism opposed settler rule, but the pan-national family does not address this directly.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Pan-Germanism fed Nazi policy, whereas Pan-African and Slavic democrats would agree; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Pan-Africanism arose from resistance to enslavement, so it would reject minimising slavery's role.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Pan-African and Pan-Arab thinkers opposed outside political models and sought their own forms such as Arab socialism and African unity governments.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nasser's Free Officers and Ba'athist coups gave the army a political role, whereas Euro-Slavs and others did not; split.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred traditionalism is not documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nkrumah's neo-colonialism critique implies blocking foreign control of key sectors; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Ba'ath charter said wealth belongs to the nation, but not that land tenure depends on use; split.

single-official-language.rationale: Arab nationalists make Arabic the common language, while Austro-Slavs, Africans and Yugoslav unionists accepted several languages; split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The OAU backed liberation movements and Pan-Arab states backed Palestinian groups, but Euro-Slavs would reject it; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Russian Pan-Slavism and Pan-Germanism had hegemonic aspects, but Pan-Africanism and Euro-Slavism oppose it; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Anti-neo-colonial strands might favour it, but it is not stated.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The ideology demands loyalty to the national community; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Pan-nationalism seeks to build large unified states or unions with active roles, the opposite of a minimal state.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Unification was pursued by force in several strands, and the family does not hold a non-aggression principle.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nkrumah proposed pooling defence, foreign policy and currency in a continental union, and the African Union and Arab League are regional pooling projects; strands that want a single state go further.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Pan-nationalists favour common defence among kin states, such as Nkrumah's African high command; ending alliances is not a doctrine, though non-alignment appeals to anti-Western strands.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-nationalism is the project of uniting a nation divided among states, and Aflaq called Arab divisions illegitimate and Pan-Arabists condemned Sykes-Picot, while Nkrumah called colonial boundaries a source of conflict.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-German annexations contrast with Arab views on Israeli annexation.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The article defines pan-nationalism as nationalism seeking a broader identity and union across existing boundaries for peoples of shared ancestry, as in Kollar's Slavs and Pan-German unity.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-colonial strands (Nkrumah) reject outside interference while Pan-German and Pan-Slav expansionists justified intervention, so adherents split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation is not addressed by the pan-national idea; adherents follow their regime's economic line.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from the family's focus on shared kinship and solidarity, though some Pan-German strands did blame minorities; not a pan-nationalist doctrine.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist and nation-building outlook of most strands; the idea itself does not address marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: No pan-national doctrine addresses freedom of information; it depends on the regime each strand produced.

local-production.rationale: Pan-African self-reliance aims at continental rather than local production, and other strands are silent.

informal-organisation.rationale: Pan-nationalism works through leagues, congresses, parties and unions of states, not small informal groups; inferred from those forms.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Union government above member states, as Nkrumah proposed, implies supranational authority over single-state law; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The Wikipedia overview distinguishes pan-nationalism from religion-based unity, and Pan-Arabism and Ba'athism define the nation by language and history, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The anti-colonial strands stress opposing outside domination and unity of equals, though Russian Pan-Slavism accepted a leading Russia; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Nkrumah proposed continental common planning and currency, suggesting pooled resources; other strands are silent, so low.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: No pan-national doctrine addresses property; adherents split along their regime's economic line.

defeat-communism.rationale: Strands diverge: Arab and African socialists were non-aligned, while Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives were anti-communist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Adherents split along their economic line; the doctrine concerns national scale, not service delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ba'athists were secular while Pan-Slavism leaned on Orthodoxy and Pan-Germanism on Romantic culture, so adherents split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Socialist strands like Nkrumah's reject capitalism while conservative strands accept it; the family has no shared view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Arab and African socialist strands might agree while Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives would not; adherents split.

socialized-care.rationale: The doctrine does not address domestic work; strands split along their social line.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Pan-Germanist purism (Jahn, Arndt) contrasts with strands that use a colonial language as common tongue; adherents split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns relations across borders, not with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The family aims at larger unions of peoples, not small self-governing communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-German settlement policy contrasts with strands that have no such programme.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Aflaq and Nkrumah sought a socialist third course but Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives did not; adherents split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Unity claims rest on shared ancestry and homeland, as in Greater Germany and Pan-Slav claims, though adherents differ; inferred from the family's ethnic-territorial logic.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Pan-nationalism says nothing on the Holocaust; adherents range from Pan-German nationalists to anti-colonial Africans, and most mainstream strands would not deny it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split by regime and strand, from African states with such laws to secular Arab and Slavic ones.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ba'athist vanguard rule suppressed opponents while Pan-Slav and Pan-African figures were mixed; the shared core takes no position.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Orthodox Pan-Slavs favoured established religion while secular Ba'athists did not; the core of unity across borders is silent.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The anti-colonial strands (Pan-Africanism, Pan-Arabism) are defined by opposing outside domination and neo-colonialism, as Nkrumah argued in 1963.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Pan-Islamism is explicitly excluded from the profile; ethnic pan-nationalists do not ground resistance in a religious duty. Inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The profile is ethnic not religious and the Ba'ath was secular, so religious-law legitimacy is not a core claim; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Nkrumah's continental planning was centralised while 1848 Pan-Slavs sought national assemblies; no shared doctrine on direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; the family focuses on nation and borders, and adherents split by strand.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed by any pan-nationalist doctrine; adherents split widely.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by any pan-nationalist doctrine; adherents split widely.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nationalism claims to transcend class, but Arab socialists and Pan-German conservatives sit on different sides; no shared position.

alienated-labor.rationale: Ba'athist and African socialists may agree while Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives would not; the shared core is silent.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Pan-Slavs and Pan-Germans sometimes held such views while Pan-Arabs and Pan-Africans did not; no shared position.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ba'athism was secular and Nkrumah's Pan-Africanism rested on the people, but Orthodox Pan-Slavs and monarchist strands differ; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secular Ba'athism favoured it while other strands did not; the shared core is silent.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The family spans socialist planners and conservatives and has no shared economic model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Nkrumah called for a continental union government with a common defence, so adherents favour combined rather than abolished armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Nkrumah urged collective continental planning for industrial development rather than leaving some regions to grow first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Nasser's Arab and African unity movements embraced non-alignment between the Cold War blocs, though Pan-Germanism and Pan-Slavism were aligned with great powers.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Pan-nationalism is about unity across borders, not how office is passed on; pan-Slav and pan-German monarchists would agree while Ba'athists and Nkrumahists would not.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Pan-national doctrine says nothing about credit; adherents split along their regime's economic line.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial strands (Nkrumah, Nasser) that oppose outside economic domination, though other strands never addressed it.

property-franchise.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; conservative strands favoured limited franchises while Arab and African strands favoured mass suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The doctrine is silent on ecology and gender; adherents' views follow their wider ideology.

reification.rationale: Not addressed by pan-nationalism; only its socialist strands would use the idea.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; socialist strands would agree and conservative or liberal strands would not.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not a pan-national question; adherents ranged from constitutional liberals in 1848 to single-party rulers.

racial-franchise.rationale: The source distinguishes pan-nationalism from race-based doctrines, and the Ba'ath and Pan-Africanism are explicitly multi-religious or continental, so a single-group franchise is not its core; Pan-German racial strands dissent.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic for a doctrine of the 19th and 20th centuries; no stated position.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; adherents' views follow their regime's openness.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Adherents split: secular Ba'athists reject religious barriers while some Pan-Slav and Pan-German strands tied nation to church.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from strands such as Ba'athism, led by a Christian-born founder and uniting Arabs of all faiths, which oppose communal division within the nation.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The family centres on the scale of the nation, not on how decisions are made; Pan-African and Arab socialist strands might welcome popular deliberation while Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives would not.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Pan-nationalism is ethnic and cultural rather than religious, so adherents split between secular modernisers (Ba'athists) and religious traditionalists; inferred from the scope, which excludes Pan-Islamism.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The family is about the scale of the nation, not economics; Arab socialists and Nkrumah's followers would agree while conservative strands would not.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Pan-nationalists are split across strands and eras on gay rights, and the shared core says nothing on it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Most strands are secular or religiously traditional rather than atheist-promoting; Ba'athism is secular but none of the sources show a push for state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Unity projects aim to build or strengthen shared institutions, so abolishing police and prisons is inferred to be rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The core aim is unity of one people across borders, which is inferred to cut against dividing power between communities, though federal unions are accepted.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core; strands disagree on state versus private help for the poor.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the family has no shared position on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; strands range from democratic Pan-Africanists to authoritarian Ba'athists.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutrality is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Strands differ, from secular Ba'athists to religiously traditional Pan-Slavs, and the core is silent.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core; strands differ on family and gender order.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Split: strands stress kinship across borders, but the family offers no common view on non-kin residents.

rent-control.rationale: Split by strand: Ba'athist and Nasserist socialism would accept rent caps, while Pan-Germanism had no such programme.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the family says nothing on intellectual property, and its mostly state-led economics lean against abolition.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: Jahn's Pan-German gymnastics clubs and the Ba'ath's youth organisations drilled the young for the national cause.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Split: Pan-African statements favoured keeping Africa free of nuclear arms, but other strands did not address it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-colonial strands such as Nkrumah's and the Ba'ath oppose foreign military domination of the region.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the family; strands differ.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the socialist leanings of Nkrumah, Nasser and the Ba'ath, though Pan-Germanism differs.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the family treats force as legitimate for unification and liberation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The family holds that peoples sharing ancestry, language and culture form one nation with common origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the largely conventional social views of the historical strands.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the largely conventional social views of the historical strands.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: Ba'athist and Pan-German movements honour those who died for the nation or cause.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Split: Pan-Slavism had an Orthodox messianic strand and Aflaq stressed a spiritual Arab mission, while Nkrumah's was secular.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: unity across states gathers the people in one polity rather than leaving a diaspora centred on a homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: Split: Pan-Slavism began with Kollar's cultural programme, but Nkrumah urged seeking the political kingdom first.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conventional religious views of the historical strands.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conventional religious views of the historical strands.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Split: anti-colonial strands want local control of the economy, but the family has no common line on majority and minority groups.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Its defining aim is to merge the divided parts of a people across state borders into one unit, as in Nkrumah's call for African union.

independent-unions.rationale: The family spans Arab socialists and conservative Pan-Germans, so there is no shared position on unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Arab socialist and Nkrumahist strands agree, while Pan-Slav and Pan-German conservatives do not.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Strands split between socialist public ownership and conservative or liberal economics.

second-chamber.rationale: The family has no shared view on legislative design; unions of states take many forms.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the ideology works at the scale of the whole people or union, not the locality, and local-ownership models are not part of it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Federal unions are one aim, but the statement's delegates-do-not-govern model contradicts the centralising strands, so adherents split.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The sources are silent on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The sources are silent on ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The sources are silent on payment privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: The sources are silent on online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the priority given to the people as a unit over its members, though Pan-Africanist liberation strands stress individual rights too.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Pan-Arabism has secular and Islamic strands and Pan-Slavism an Orthodox one, so the family is split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Strands differ on federalism versus a unitary state, so adherents are split.

gm-crops.rationale: The sources are silent on GM crops.

dense-cities.rationale: The sources are silent on urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Pan-Africanism and Pan-Germanism lean on race or ancestry, while Pan-Arabism and Pan-Slavism stress language and culture, so the family is split.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in shared ancestry features in some strands and is disowned by others, so adherents are split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Anti-colonial strands emphasise defence, while Pan-German and Pan-Slav strands accepted expansion, so adherents are split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Slavism, Pan-Germanism and Pan-Arabism all define the nation by shared language and culture across state borders, though Pan-Africanism rests more on shared history and anti-colonial solidarity.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the aim of one unified people; the Ba'ath charter is secular and treats the nation as a single body, so separate religious electorates would divide it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial strands, which read Sykes-Picot and colonial borders as imperial divisions and warn of neo-colonialism; strands differ on how far this is a plot.

free-public-college.rationale: Pan-nationalism has no doctrine on tuition; adherents follow their regime's economic line.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is outside the doctrine and adherents split along economic lines.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the idea of a people's continuity across generations, though no strand makes this a stated aim.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by pan-nationalist doctrine; the strands differ on gender roles.

arms-reduction.rationale: Nkrumah called for a common continental defence, so the family does not clearly favour lower armaments.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial strands, which condemned secret imperial agreements such as Sykes-Picot, though the doctrine does not address diplomatic method.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's call for common planning and the Ba'ath socialist articles; the Pan-German and Pan-Slav strands did not share this.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Pan-nationalist states aim to build unified states with central control of force, but the sources do not address arms; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Pan-nationalists seek unification through struggle and mobilise armies, though anti-colonial strands oppose wars among brother states; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Arab socialists and Nkrumah favour labour rights while Pan-German conservatives do not; the family has no shared line.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The ideology concerns the scale of the nation, not tax policy; strands diverge widely.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Anti-colonial pan-nationalists favour state-led development with large public spending, so binding fiscal limits are disfavoured; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Nkrumah and the Ba'ath argue for ending neocolonial economic domination, though the Pan-German and Pan-Slav strands lacked this concern.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pan-nationalists generally seek to build or capture strong unified states rather than smash them, though revolutionary Ba'athists broke the old order; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Pan-nationalists seek a unified political economy, though Nkrumah allowed varied national paths in the short term; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The sources are silent on environmental accounting; strands diverge.

sacred-nation.rationale: Pan-nationalism treats the supranational nation as an enduring community with its own mission, as in Aflaq's Arab nation and Slavic and German romantic nationalism.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The sources are silent on student debt; adherents split by strand.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Pan-Africanists and Arab nationalists attribute underdevelopment to colonial and core-periphery exploitation; inferred from anti-colonial strands.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Romantic pan-nationalists stress differences between peoples while Nkrumah and Aflaq invoke a universal humanism; the family is split.

public-service-media.rationale: The sources do not address media policy; strands range from state-controlled Ba'athist media to free-press positions.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The family unites on language, ancestry or civilization across borders, and its strands differ on religion, so it takes no clear stand.

farm-price-support.rationale: Economics varies widely between strands, from Ba'athist socialism to Pan-German conservatism, so adherents split.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The sources do not address nuclear weapons, and strands differ on armament; the family offers no common view.

workers-own-party.rationale: Ba'athism and Nkrumah's Pan-Africanism lean left, while Pan-Germanism did not, so adherents split on class-based parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: The family is about unity across borders, not social practices, and its strands differ on custom and law.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Secular strands such as the Ba'ath and Nkrumah's Pan-Africanism favour legal equality, but the family has no shared doctrine on inheritance; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Pan-Slavism and Pan-Arabism treat dialects across regions as one language of one people, as the basis for unity, though some strands do not stress it. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The family has no common position on environmental law or the courts.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Pan-Africanism has room for chiefs while other strands are modernising and centralising, so adherents split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The family does not address environmental policy; strands differ.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Criminal justice is outside the shared core of the family, so adherents are split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Some strands, such as Pan-Germanism, stress a common language, but the anti-colonial strands are open on language of migrants; the family does not settle it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The family has no shared economic doctrine; strands range from Ba'athist and Nkrumahist socialism to German and Slavic conservatism, so neutral is inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Pan-nationalism concerns unity across borders and says nothing on electoral administration; strands differ, so neutral is inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Strands differ widely: Ba'athism was secular, Pan-Slavism leaned on Orthodoxy and Pan-Germanism varied; the shared core is silent, so neutral is inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The shared core is unity, not regime type; strands include democratic federations and one-party Ba'athist or Nasserist rule, so adherents are genuinely split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Most historical strands were socially conservative on sexual morality, though Ba'athism was secular; inferred, as the shared core does not address it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; strands span both free-expression and order-first regimes, so neutral is inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: No shared welfare doctrine; strands run from socialist to conservative, so the question splits adherents and neutral is inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The anti-colonial strands (Pan-Africanism, Ba'athism) accepted women's political participation in principle, and the shared core does not oppose it; inferred, with older strands mixed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Most strands treat religion as part of a shared cultural identity, so adherents would not call it a main cause of oppression, though secular Ba'athists might; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Pan-Germanism and some Pan-Slavism drew on ancestry or race, while Pan-Africanism and Pan-Arabism stress shared history and culture; adherents are genuinely split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core; socialist strands might favour such bodies and conservative ones not, so neutral is inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the unity doctrine; the strands (Pan-Slav, Pan-German, Pan-Arab, Pan-African) hold different property theories, so none is inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The family is about unity and anti-domination, not international law; anti-colonial strands distrust outside courts while others never addressed them, so adherents are split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Religion divides the family: Orthodox Pan-Slavs and secular Ba'athists or Nkrumahists differ, so no common answer exists.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core; the strands differ on gender equality and Indigenous self-government is not their frame.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Arab socialists and Nkrumah's planning followers might agree while Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives would not; the statement is outside the shared core.

indirect-election.rationale: Nkrumah's union government and the Ba'ath vanguard suggest some indirectness, but Pan-Germans and others favoured other forms; adherents are split.

national-church-status.rationale: Pan-Slavism often leaned on Orthodoxy while Pan-Arabism and Pan-Africanism were secular or multi-faith, so the family has no common view.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Pan-nationalism wants a people unified across borders; whether its own minorities within other states get autonomy varies by strand (Austro-Slavs for, Pan-Germans differently).

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Self-determination by vote fits some strands, but Pan-German and Pan-Arab claims rested on ethnic or cultural unity rather than local ballots, so adherents are split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Nkrumah called colonial boundary disputes a sore that only union could heal and Aflaq rejected Arab divisions, so adherents see colonial borders as artificial; the OAU's later acceptance of them was a compromise.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; the family has no shared view on lifestyle or consumption.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Indigenous settlement is not addressed by the shared core, and strands that claim a single nation across borders would not obviously restrict movement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription is not a defining issue; Pan-German and Pan-Arab states conscripted men, but no strand takes a documented view on equal application.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: Pan-Slav and Pan-German thinkers appealed to ancestral land and common descent, though Pan-African and Pan-Arab strands stress shared civilization more than land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the family concerns unity across borders and has no doctrine on drug policy; most strands would reject killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: anti-colonial strands favour non-alignment, but the family has no position on China specifically.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Unity of a people across state borders is the core claim; Pan-Germanism and Pan-Slavism both aimed to bring kin peoples under one roof.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the family; socialist strands such as Nkrumah's might agree while conservative strands would not.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the family; individualist and collectivist strands disagree.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the family; economic views vary widely among strands.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed by the family; welfare views vary from Arab socialism to Pan-German conservatism.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Split: Ba'athist and Nasserist strands favoured a leader or single party, while other strands were parliamentary.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not addressed by the family; strands are split on economics.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Split: Pan-Arabism was secular and cross-confessional, while Pan-Slavism often leaned on Orthodoxy.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Split: Pan-German romantics prized ancestral values, while Nkrumah's Pan-Africanism stressed modernisation.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed by the family; strands are split on social questions.

national-resource-control.rationale: The anti-colonial strands, Nkrumah and the Ba'ath, demanded control of national resources against foreign domination.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The family is about the scale of the nation, not distributive justice, and strands span socialist Ba'athists to conservative Pan-Germans.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: No pan-national doctrine addresses it; adherents split along their regime's economic line.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Strands range from anti-colonial Pan-Africanism, which stresses racism, to racial Pan-Germanism, so adherents are split.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The sources give no common position on law's authority; strands differ widely on democracy and religion.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed by any pan-national doctrine, and strands differ on economics.

multipolar-world.rationale: Larger unions are meant to stand against outside domination, as in Nkrumah's call for continental union against neo-colonialism and Aflaq's Arab unity, though not every strand states it as a world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Ba'athist and African socialists may hold labour-based views while Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives do not, so the family is split.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Ba'athism and Nkrumah's Pan-Africanism link unity with socialism, but Pan-German and Pan-Slav conservatives do not, so adherents split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Pan-nationalism is itself an identity politics, while its socialist strands stress material aims, so no common side.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The Ba'ath vanguard party and Nkrumah's planning point toward party-led socialism, but most strands are not communist, so the family is split.

missingStatements.text: Colonial-era borders should be treated as artificial and should be dissolved into a larger union of the peoples they divided.
missingStatements.rationale: Nkrumah called boundary disputes a festering sore that only unity could heal, and Aflaq rejected Arab divisions; existing statements only partly capture the border-dissolving claim.

notes: The answers are for the shared core of a heterogeneous family. Ba'athism and Nkrumahism are socialist, Pan-Germanism turned imperialist and racist, Pan-Slavism split into Austro-Slavism, democratic Euro-Slavism and Russian-led Pan-Slavism. Statements about economics, democracy and religion are therefore largely neutral or low-confidence; an audit of an individual strand would give more definite answers.
